title: Read real classical themes
description: A compact path through exact source passages: Ode to Joy soprano-line reading, then the published Blue Danube main-theme piano arrangement. These are two verified source variants, not a complete beginner piano method.

policies.notes: Exact source notes, rhythms, chords, rests and ties; never generated, simplified or transposed.
policies.practiceModes: Hand/voice isolation and smaller passages filter the same canonical source. They are not different difficulty arrangements.
policies.fingering: Both included sources supply no fingering. Omit all finger numbers and inferred movement instructions.
policies.tempo: Learning tempo changes playback speed only; preserve source meter and relative durations.
policies.prerequisites: Skill requirements describe the passage. Support a learner readiness check; do not gate by an arbitrary global lesson index.
policies.progress: Keep variant, passage/whole, hand/voice, input and timing modes separate. Section completion does not complete the whole score.
policies.assessment: MIDI can check enabled note/timing rules; microphone supports monophonic pitch study only. No input certifies fingering, posture or physical ease.
policies.legacy: Do not award these source passages from legacy generated-curriculum completions.

readinessGap: This path has a genuine jump from monophonic reading to the dyads and bass/chord patterns of the Blue Danube edition. It does not pretend to supply a complete primer. Offer external already-published beginner piano resources while more suitable source permissions are established.

stages.title: Read a familiar melody
stages.description: Begin with exact soprano-line excerpts from an SATB Ode to Joy source. This is melody reading on a piano, not a complete published piano arrangement.

stages.title: Read the rhythm and phrase
stages.description: Retain dotted notes, eighth notes, phrase endings and changes of register. Slow the same source passage without changing its notation.

stages.title: Read the real waltz parts
stages.description: Read the actual bass, chords and upper-staff dyads of the published Blue Danube main-theme piano arrangement.

stages.title: Connect the waltz phrases
stages.description: Prepare the next hand location and harmony, then join source phrases on a steady three-beat pulse.

stages.title: Read the ending and play the theme
stages.description: Keep tied notes sounding over the accompaniment, read the written accidental and dotted rhythm, and assemble the complete selected arrangement.

skills.description: Find a written starting note on the keyboard
Read repeated notes and steps in treble clef
Count a dotted quarter followed by an eighth note
Hear and read a phrase ending
Prepare a new register without holding a fixed stretch
Connect source phrases while reading changed endings
Count all three beats in a 3/4 bar
Read bass-clef starting notes and chord locations
Play the written bass note and repeated chord pattern
Read and play written two-note chords together
Keep each hand's written entry and duration
Prepare the next source harmony and hand location
Hold tied melody notes while the other hand continues
Apply the source accidental at the correct note
Keep counting through a written ending rest
Connect the complete selected main-theme arrangement

nextRepertoire.instructions: Select another already-created online variant after inspecting its exact notation, permissions and first new demands. Advanced originals and the remaining 37-piece target catalogue remain separate from this playable starter path.

lessons.title: Ode to Joy: the first written notes
lessons.objective: Read repeated notes and steps in the exact opening three-bar fragment.

guide.beforePlaying: Find B4, the written first note. The fragment stays between G4 and D5. The source is in G major; these three bars do not sound F-sharp.
practiceSteps: Listen once and follow the treble notes from left to right.
Find B4, then point out a repeated note and a downward step in the score.
Play the three bars with an easy quarter-note pulse; use note-wait mode only to find uncertain notes.
guide.listenFor: Repeated pitches need separate attacks. Every note in this fragment lasts one quarter-note beat.
guide.readyWhen: You can find the starting key, read the repeated notes and steps, and keep the short fragment moving slowly.
guide.sourceNote: This is an unchanged soprano line from an SATB setting, played on piano. Three bars are an opening fragment, not the complete phrase or a novice piano edition.

lessons.title: Finish the first Ode phrase
lessons.objective: Count the source dotted-quarter/eighth ending and its half note.

guide.beforePlaying: Look at bar 4 before starting. Its dotted quarter lasts one-and-a-half beats, the following eighth lasts half a beat, and the half note lasts two beats.
practiceSteps: Tap an even subdivided count while listening to bar 4.
Play the written bar 4 slowly, then connect bars 3–4 without changing their rhythm.
Play bars 1–4 and listen for the phrase ending.
guide.listenFor: The short eighth note follows the longer dotted quarter; the last note spans two beats.
guide.readyWhen: You can count the ending as written and reach it without replacing its rhythm with equal notes.

lessons.title: Read the changed answer
lessons.objective: Recognise the repeated opening and read its different ending.

guide.beforePlaying: Compare bar 8 with bar 4. Read the answer before playing it from memory.
practiceSteps: Point to the notes that differ at the ending.
Play the answer with the written dotted rhythm.
Listen for its arrival on G and compare it with the first phrase.
guide.listenFor: The source supplies the variation; the changed ending should be audible.
guide.readyWhen: You can play the written answer and identify how its ending differs from the first phrase.

lessons.title: Connect the first two Ode phrases
lessons.objective: Read the complete eight-bar opening and keep its two different phrase endings.

guide.beforePlaying: Compare the ending at source bar 4 with bar 8. The first ends on A4; the answer arrives on G4.
practiceSteps: Preview the changed notes at the two endings.
Play source bars 1–8 continuously, retaining the dotted-quarter/eighth figures and half notes.
Repair the join between bars 4 and 5, then reconnect the entire eight-bar opening.
guide.listenFor: The second phrase answers the first without an extra pause between them.
guide.readyWhen: You can connect both phrases and retain their distinct endings.

lessons.title: Follow the middle phrase and its register change
lessons.objective: Read the written eighth-note groups and prepare the lower D4.

guide.beforePlaying: Find the eighth notes at bars 10–11. Bar 12 ends on D4, below the opening G4–D5 region; locate that destination before playing.
practiceSteps: Tap the paired eighth notes evenly inside the beat.
Read the last bar and silently locate D4.
Play the complete middle phrase slowly, allowing the hand to travel rather than holding a fixed stretch.
guide.listenFor: Two eighth notes fit into one beat. The register change does not add an unwritten pause.
guide.readyWhen: You can keep the subdivisions even and prepare the lower final note before reaching it.
guide.sourceNote: The complete soprano line does not remain in one five-finger position. This edition supplies no fingering.

lessons.title: Read the return
lessons.objective: Read the familiar return and retain its exact ending.

guide.beforePlaying: Compare this phrase with bars 5–8 and notice what returns.
practiceSteps: Preview the first note and final rhythm.
Play the return as written, with the same steady pulse used for the earlier phrases.
Listen to the ending before joining the whole line.
guide.listenFor: Recognition should help you look ahead, while the score still controls the notes and rhythm.
guide.readyWhen: You can read the return without adding notes or changing its ending.

lessons.title: Connect the middle phrase to the return
lessons.objective: Read eight continuous source bars through the lower D4 and back into the return.

guide.beforePlaying: Locate the final D4 of source bar 12 and the B4 at bar 13. Prepare that upward move before joining the phrases.
practiceSteps: Preview the paired eighths in bars 10–11 and the register change at bars 12–13.
Play source bars 9–16 at a tempo that keeps the eighths even.
Repair the bar-12-to-13 transition, then reconnect the full eight-bar passage.
guide.listenFor: The middle phrase and familiar return share one pulse despite the change of register.
guide.readyWhen: You can connect the eight bars without adding a pause or altering the final dotted rhythm.

lessons.title: Play the complete selected Ode melody line
lessons.objective: Connect all four source phrases into the complete 16-bar soprano line.

guide.beforePlaying: Preview the phrase boundaries after bars 4, 8 and 12, and the lower destination in bar 12.
practiceSteps: Choose a tempo at which the middle phrase remains comfortable.
Play all 16 bars, keeping the written values and phrasing.
Choose one uncertain bar, correct it, and reconnect it to its phrase.
guide.listenFor: A continuous pulse across phrase boundaries and the written differences between the endings.
guide.readyWhen: You can connect the line coherently, identify one specific improvement and demonstrate that correction.
guide.sourceNote: Completion means this soprano-line study. It does not certify a full piano arrangement of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.

lessons.title: Find the Blue Danube pickup and three-beat pulse
lessons.objective: Locate the exact opening fragment and count the pickup into 3/4.

guide.beforePlaying: Source bar 1 is a one-quarter-note pickup on C4. Source bar 2 is the first full bar: C4–E4–G4.
practiceSteps: Listen and count the pickup into “1 2 3.”
Find C4 and read the rising broken-triad contour in the full bar.
Play this exact short fragment while retaining the three-beat grouping.
guide.listenFor: The pickup leads into beat 1; it is not a complete three-beat bar.
guide.readyWhen: You can locate the pickup and count the following three-beat bar.
guide.sourceNote: This two-source-bar fragment is not the complete opening phrase. Pickup counts as source bar 1 throughout these lessons.

lessons.title: Read the real bass and chord pattern
lessons.objective: Read bass C3 and the E3/G3 dyad on beats 2 and 3.

guide.beforePlaying: Read the bass clef separately. In each selected bar the lower staff has C3 on beat 1, then E3/G3 together on beats 2 and 3.
practiceSteps: Locate C3, E3 and G3 from the bass staff.
Prepare the two-note chord silently, then play one source bar with three clear beats.
Play all four bars, letting the key rise before each repeated chord attack.
guide.listenFor: A lower bass note followed by two simultaneous-note chords; each chord is a single attack, not a broken chord.
guide.readyWhen: You can keep all three beats clear and sound both notes of each written chord together.
guide.sourceNote: The app checks the source notes and supported timing. This edition has no finger numbers; MIDI cannot identify your chosen fingers.

lessons.title: Prepare the opening melody and dyads
lessons.objective: Read the written move into the upper dyads and sustain the half notes.

guide.beforePlaying: After the low C–E–G opening, source bar 3 introduces an E5/G5 dyad. Locate that upper group without holding the hand stretched from the starting key.
practiceSteps: Preview the starting note and the first upper dyad.
Play slowly through the move, keeping each two-note chord simultaneous.
Connect the full opening phrase with its written half-note durations.
guide.listenFor: The melody moves into a higher register; half notes last two beats even when a later note is being prepared.
guide.readyWhen: You can prepare the higher group and retain the written durations through the phrase.

lessons.title: Join the hands at the written entry
lessons.objective: Coordinate the source left-hand entry with the held right-hand melody.

guide.beforePlaying: The lower staff rests through source bars 1–2 and enters at bar 3. The right hand holds a half note while the left hand continues its beat pattern.
practiceSteps: Review each hand alone at the same comfortable tempo.
Count through the left-hand rests and enter only at the written place.
Keep the right-hand half note sounding while the left-hand beat pattern continues, then finish the phrase.
guide.listenFor: The hands have different jobs and do not always strike together.
guide.readyWhen: Both hands keep their own written attacks and durations without an unexpected stop.

lessons.title: Read the first changed harmony
lessons.objective: Follow the repeated opening into its different chord answer.

guide.beforePlaying: Compare the dyads and lower-staff harmony with the first phrase. Preview the new group before playing.
practiceSteps: Read each hand separately and locate the new chord shapes.
Play the exact passage slowly with three beats per full bar.
Reconnect it after the first phrase and keep the accompaniment even.
guide.listenFor: A recognisable opening with a changed harmonic answer.
guide.readyWhen: You can prepare the new harmony and connect the phrase without changing the source notes.

lessons.title: Read the B–D–A motif
lessons.objective: Prepare the new melodic shape and upper chord locations.

guide.beforePlaying: The new source motif rises B–D–A. Its entry note is already heard on the final beat of source bar 9; listen to that connection before starting this bar-range study.
practiceSteps: Preview the new starting location and the upper dyads.
Play each hand alone if the move is uncertain.
Play the selected bars, then reconnect the entry from the preceding phrase.
guide.listenFor: The new contour remains inside the same three-beat pulse.
guide.readyWhen: You can locate the new group in advance and keep the phrase moving.

lessons.title: Read the changed answer to the second motif
lessons.objective: Read the related motif with its source-defined different ending.

guide.beforePlaying: Compare this answer with source bars 10–13. Its entry is prepared by the final beat of source bar 13.
practiceSteps: Point out the changed upper dyads and lower harmony.
Read the exact answer slowly.
Connect both versions of the motif, including their preceding entry notes.
guide.listenFor: The similar beginning and different musical arrival.
guide.readyWhen: You can keep the source endings distinct and connect each to its entry.

lessons.title: Connect the opening section
lessons.objective: Join the pickup and first four motif groups.

guide.beforePlaying: Locate the changes of motif and harmony before starting. Keep the pickup and all lower-staff rests.
practiceSteps: Choose the tempo from your least secure phrase.
Play source bars 1–17 as one connected section.
Review one transition and reconnect the neighbouring phrases.
guide.listenFor: A continuous waltz pulse across the joins, with the melody audible above its accompaniment.
guide.readyWhen: You can connect the section and repair a specific transition without restarting from the beginning every time.

lessons.title: Read the higher phrase
lessons.objective: Move the same rising outline into its higher source register.

guide.beforePlaying: Read the higher right-hand group and the changed lower-staff location. The entry note is heard at the end of source bar 17.
practiceSteps: Silently locate each hand's new destination.
Play each part alone, retaining its written rhythm.
Join the parts and reconnect the entry from bar 17.
guide.listenFor: The same three-beat motion remains clear while the hand locations change.
guide.readyWhen: You can prepare both destinations and play the phrase without holding an unnecessary stretch.

lessons.title: Read the higher answer and sustained chord
lessons.objective: Follow the changed harmony into the source bar-25 held chord.

guide.beforePlaying: Source bar 25 contains a sustained lower-staff chord. Read its duration rather than continuing the earlier repeated pattern automatically.
practiceSteps: Compare the accompaniment in bar 25 with the preceding bars.
Play the exact lower-staff change alone.
Join the hands, then connect the passage to the preceding phrase.
guide.listenFor: The written held chord replaces the repeated accompaniment at its actual location.
guide.readyWhen: You can change the accompaniment texture without adding unwritten repeated attacks.

lessons.title: Read the tied melody before joining the bass
lessons.objective: Read the exact upper-staff ties and F-sharp before adding the moving accompaniment.

guide.beforePlaying: Source bars 27–28 tie A4; bars 29–30 tie E5. The tied continuations need no new attack. F-sharp at bar 28 is a separate note.
practiceSteps: Play the right-hand source line alone and hold each tie across its bar line.
Find the written F-sharp in bar 28 and its following G4.
Keep the full five-bar pulse before joining the same passage with the source left hand.
guide.listenFor: Two sustained notes cross bar lines; the F-sharp and following G remain separate attacks.
guide.readyWhen: You can sustain both ties and read F-sharp without adding attacks at the tied continuations.

lessons.title: Hold the melody while the bass moves
lessons.objective: Retain the tied melody, changing accompaniment and written F-sharp.

guide.beforePlaying: Find the tie between bars 27–28, the F-sharp in bar 28 and the tie between 29–30. A tie continues a note; it does not request another strike.
practiceSteps: Read the upper line alone and identify which noteheads are tied continuations.
Locate F-sharp and listen to its move to G.
Join the hands, keeping tied notes sounding while the left hand plays its own attacks.
guide.listenFor: The held melody continues across the bar line without retriggering, while the lower staff remains active.
guide.readyWhen: You can hold the ties, read the accidental and retain the left-hand rhythm.

lessons.title: Read the written cadence and ending rest
lessons.objective: Read the final chords, dotted-quarter/eighth figure and rest.

guide.beforePlaying: Source bar 33 contains the dotted-quarter/eighth detail. Source bar 34 has its final attack followed by a half rest; continue counting through that silence.
practiceSteps: Read and tap bar 33 before playing.
Play the sustained lower-staff chords with their written durations.
Join the hands through the final attack and count the remaining rest.
guide.listenFor: The cadence keeps its dotted rhythm, and the silence belongs to the written ending.
guide.readyWhen: You can keep the final rhythm and end with the rest rather than adding another note.

lessons.title: Connect the second section
lessons.objective: Join the higher phrases, tied line and cadence.

guide.beforePlaying: Preview the register changes, source bar-25 texture change, ties, accidental and final dotted rhythm.
practiceSteps: Choose a tempo that keeps the cadence and ties secure.
Play source bars 18–34 with independent hand durations.
Correct one transition and reconnect its neighbouring bars.
guide.listenFor: A continuous pulse through changes of register, texture and note value.
guide.readyWhen: You can connect the second section and retain the specific details identified in the preview.

lessons.title: Play the complete published Blue Danube main theme
lessons.objective: Connect the complete N. Kouremenos main-theme piano arrangement.

guide.beforePlaying: This selected edition has a one-beat pickup followed by 33 full 3/4 bars. Choose a comfortable learning tempo; the source MIDI tempo is not an entry requirement.
practiceSteps: Preview the phrase joins and your most uncertain transition.
Play the complete selected arrangement with its written notes, chords, rests, ties and dynamics.
Identify one musical or technical improvement, practise its exact location, then reconnect it to the phrase.
guide.listenFor: The waltz pulse, clear melody and the different phrase arrivals across the complete selected theme.
guide.readyWhen: You can give a coherent slow performance, name a specific improvement and demonstrate the correction. Comfortable movement and expression remain listening/self/teacher judgments.
guide.sourceNote: This completes the published main-theme piano arrangement, not the complete orchestral waltz Op. 314. No fingering is supplied by this edition.
